verified.kill_fact: PRIMARY-SOURCE CHECK (8-K filed 2026-08-24, SEC Accession 0001193125-26-363681): the core facts hold — Hub Group is out of compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5250(c)(1), received "a 180-day exception period, or until September 14, 2026," to file the delinquent FY2025 10-K and Q1 2026 10-Q (Q2 10-Q also delinquent, NT 10-Q filed 2026-08-11), and as of 2026-09-06 EDGAR shows NO 10-K, NO 10-Q and no 8-K after 08-24, so the catalyst is genuinely unfired 8 days out. "Non-extendable ... delisting" is wrong: under Nasdaq Rule 5810(c)(2)/5815, 180 days is the maximum the STAFF may grant, not the maximum the company may remain listed. A miss on 09-14 produces a Staff Delisting Determination that the company can appeal to a Hearings Panel; the appeal STAYS suspension and the Panel may keep the security listed up to 360 calendar days from the original filing due date (~2026-03-17 → ~2027-03-12). So 09-14 is not a cliff, it is a checkpoint — which guts the asymmetry the thesis is built on in both directions: there is no forced-delisting downside to be relieved, and therefore no mechanical reason a "delisting discount" must close that day. Second correction: the numerator has no provenance. Third: the event is two-sided information release, not discount removal — a clean 09-14 file dumps restated FY23-25, Q1 and Q2 2026 numbers plus an adverse ICFR opinion simultaneously, and the stated restatement scope could not be confirmed as still $77M. Real, cheap, unfired, correctly dated — but the "binary, mechanical, non-extendable" premise that justified a 6 does not survive the rule text.
